subject: social
title: History Detectives
about: Asking questions, telling facts from opinions, who made a book, and primary versus secondary sources (diaries, old photos, artifacts, museums). NC inquiry I.1.1, I.1.6, I.1.7 and 1.H.1.2.
tip: At dinner, take turns saying one fact and one opinion about the meal.

cards.q: What do we ask when we want to learn something?
cards.note: Good detectives ask who, what, when, where and why.

cards.q: What do we call something that is true and you can check?
cards.note: You can check a fact by counting or looking.

cards.q: What do we call what someone thinks or feels about something?
cards.note: People can have different opinions, and that is okay.

cards.q: 'Pizza is the best food.' Is that a fact or an opinion?
cards.note: It is an opinion because someone else might like tacos best.

cards.q: 'A week has seven days.' Is that a fact or an opinion?
cards.note: It is a fact because you can count the days on a calendar.

cards.q: 'Dogs are the best pets.' Is that a fact or an opinion?
cards.note: It is an opinion because someone else might think cats are the best pets.

cards.q: 'A cat has four legs.' Is that a fact or an opinion?
cards.note: It is a fact because you can count the legs on a cat.

cards.q: Who writes the words in a book?
cards.note: The author's name is usually on the front of the book.

cards.q: Who draws the pictures in a book?
cards.note: Sometimes one person is both the author and the illustrator.

cards.q: When we look at an old book or photo, we ask who made it, when, where, and what else?
cards.note: Who, when, where and why help us understand a source, like a book, a photo or a diary.

cards.q: What do we call something made by a person who was there, like a diary or an old photo?
cards.note: A primary source comes straight from someone who was there.

cards.q: What do we call something made later by someone who was not there, like a textbook?
cards.note: A secondary source tells about the past by using other sources.

cards.q: Is an old diary a primary source or a secondary source?
cards.note: The person who wrote the diary was there, so it is a primary source.

cards.q: Is an encyclopedia a primary source or a secondary source?
cards.note: An encyclopedia is a big book of facts written later by people who were not there.

cards.q: Is a photo taken long ago a primary source or a secondary source?
cards.note: The person who took the photo was there, so it is a primary source.

cards.q: What do we call an old object from the past, like a tool or a toy?
cards.note: Artifacts help us learn how people lived long ago.

cards.q: What do we call a place that keeps and shows old things from the past?
cards.note: Museums keep artifacts, old photos and art safe so everyone can see them.

cards.q: Two friends tell about the same party. What can we say about their two stories?
cards.note: Each person sees and remembers things in their own way, so detectives look at more than one source.
